newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Five million N.Koreans said near starvation.
newsitem.headline: Five million N.Koreans said near starvation.

text.p: More than five million North Koreans are near starvation and many are expected to die in coming months, an official of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) said on Friday.

Ole Gronning, IFRC's representative in Pyongyang, also told a news conference, that based on U.N. estimates of the harvest in October, the country's food deficit was expected to be worse in 1998 than in 1997.
The Federation, which links 171 national Red Cross and Red Crescent societies, ended two-day talks on Friday to seek funds for its latest emergency appeal of $18 million for North Korea.
No firm new pledges were made but South Korea's Red Cross is already providing rice and corn worth some $11 million under the five-month appeal to feed some 740,000 people in the North.

"Now we are talking about a famine in the making. We have more than five million people at the level of starvation," Gronning said. "I presume that quite a few people have died over the past few months."
Government food stocks ran out in May although some private markets operate where people barter for food, according to the Dane, who travels regularly to 19 counties in North Korea.
